Build on Fedimint Card

The card keeps spend keys and a PIN on its chip. A till builds each Fedimint transaction, the card signs its hash, and a registry records which notes belong to which card. Everything here is open source.

01

How the parts fit

One NFC tap connects the holder's card to a merchant's till. The till does the Fedimint work, and the registry keeps track of each card's notes.

Fedimint CardPayments · Issuance
NFCHTTPS or WebSocketFedimint APIOperator only

Swipe the diagram sideways to see all of it.

  • The card holderA Java Card applet on an NXP J3R180. It makes keys, guards them with a PIN and signs a 32-byte hash. With applet 3.0 it also keeps each note's amount for the offline limit. No command returns a private key.
  • POS phone merchantReads the card over NFC, takes the PIN and passes card commands to the till over its card link.
  • Till merchantcard-sidecar, a Rust service on the Fedimint client. It plans, builds and submits each payment, and its wallet receives the ecash.
  • Registry issuerA Cloudflare Worker at registry.fedimintcard.org. It records each card's notes by short id, and sees every balance (privacy).
  • Provisioner operatorThe operator's phone app. It installs the applet, sets per-card management keys and the PIN, and approves tills.
  • Federation guardiansA Fedimint federation with the mintv2 module. Its guardians check each note's signature and mark it spent.

02

Status

!

An experimental prototype. The applet and till have been tested on NXP J3R180 cards with a few phones, and have had no outside security review.

A card holds up to 32 notes, and with applet 3.0 a till takes taps offline and settles them when it reconnects. Some prices leave change the card cannot hold, and the till refuses them. Read the risks before anyone holds real value on a card.

03

The card's commands

AID F0464D4341524401, class byte B0. Slots 0 to 31 go in P1 (0 to 7 on the first 8-slot cards), and P2 is 0 unless a command says otherwise. These are the commands every version answers. Applet 3.0 adds note states, attestation and an offline limit, documented in the offline protocol.

10

GEN_KEY

slot

Makes a new BIP340 key in a slot and answers its public key. P2 = 1 replaces a used slot, which needs the PIN once a PIN is set.

> B0 10 ss 00
< x-only pubkey · 32 B 90 00
11

GET_PUB

slot

Answers the public key in a slot. The slot-0 key's last 4 bytes are the card's short id.

> B0 11 ss 00
< x-only pubkey · 32 B 90 00
12

SIGN

needs PIN

Signs a 32-byte message with a slot's key. The till sends the transaction hash, once for each note spent.

> B0 12 ss 00 20 tx_hash · 32 B
< BIP340 signature · 64 B 90 00
40

VERIFY_PIN

session

Checks the PIN and opens a signing session for this selection. Three wrong PINs block the card for good.

> B0 40 00 00 Lc PIN · 4–8 B
< 90 00  or 63 CX · 69 83
41

SET_PIN

once

Sets the first PIN. It works once per card and opens no session.

> B0 41 00 00 Lc PIN · 4–8 B
< 90 00
42

CHANGE_PIN

needs PIN

Replaces the PIN with one of the same length, after VERIFY_PIN. It ends the session.

> B0 42 00 00 Lc old PIN ‖ new PIN
< 90 00

Rules a reader has to follow

  • A verified PIN lasts one selection. A SELECT or a reset ends it, so send VERIFY_PIN and SIGN in the same selection.
  • Three wrong PINs block the card for good. There is no unblock command.
  • SIGN checks the PIN before the slot, so a reader without the PIN cannot learn which slots hold keys.
  • Signatures use fresh randomness, so the same message signed twice gives two different signatures.

Status words

  • 9000Done
  • 63CXWrong PIN, X tries left
  • 6983PIN blocked
  • 6984No PIN set
  • 6A94PIN not verified in this selection
  • 6985Refused: slot used or empty, or PIN already set
  • 6700Wrong length
  • 6B00Bad P1 or P2
  • 6D00Unknown INS
  • 6E00Wrong class byte
  • 6F00Crypto failure

04

A payment, step by step

Every note on the card is a Fedimint mintv2 note whose nonce is one slot's public key, in a power-of-two amount of msat. Gold arrows pass through the POS phone to the card.

One charge13 messages

Swipe the diagram sideways to see all of it.

  1. ReadThe till reads the card's short id, then its notes and free slots from the registry.
  2. PlanIt picks the inputs, the merchant's output and the card's change, balanced to the exact msat. Change goes to free slots.
  3. SignThe transaction uses NaiveMultisig. The card signs its tx_hash, which covers every input and output, once per note.
  4. SettleThe federation checks the signatures. The till records the outcome and the card's new notes.

05

The till API

The till listens on 127.0.0.1:9877. Any other address needs a POS token from card-sidecar till pair, sent as Authorization: Bearer.

  • POST/v1/chargeprice_msat, optional client_ref and PIN. Answers in 5 to 20 s; a repeated client_ref never spends twice.
  • POST/v1/card/balanceThe tapped card's balance, from the registry.
  • POST/v1/cards/precheck · keySetup · issueCheck a blank card, make its keys and PIN, and load its first notes.
  • WS/v1/card/linkThe POS phone's socket. The till sends card commands through it.
  • GET/v1/salesThe till's sales.
  • GET/v1/status · /v1/healthFederation, wallet balance, card link and registry state.

Errors you should handle

Every error answers {"ok":false,"error","detail"}.

  • wrong_pin403
    The PIN was wrong. The answer says how many tries are left.
  • pin_blocked423
    Three wrong PINs. The card no longer signs.
  • insufficient402
    The card holds less than the price.
  • no_exact_plan422
    The card cannot hold the change this price leaves.
  • undecided202
    The federation has not answered yet. Ask again with the same client_ref.
  • card_changed409
    The card's notes moved since the till read them.
  • busy409
    The till is in another charge.
  • ops_unreachable502
    The registry did not answer.

The till API reference has every field and error, and POS link covers the phone's side.

06

The registry

  • Operators sign in with a password for a 12-hour token. Operator accounts come only from a deploy secret, never over HTTP.
  • Tills get their own revocable tokens. A till asks with a claim code, and an operator approves it in the provisioner.
  • A till or operator sees only its own operator's cards. Any other card answers 404.
  • Each card's management keys are derived from a registry secret and kept there, for reinstalling or resetting the card.

The operations plan covers the design, and till claim the approval flow.

08

Try it

You can run the real applet and a whole federation without a card. Pick where to start.

repo root
# the applet's tests in jCardSim, then the bridge
$ mvn -B test
$ mvn -B package -DskipTests
$ java -jar bridge/target/bridge.jar --port 9876

# send it a SELECT
$ curl -s localhost:9876/apdu -d '{"apdu":"00A4040008F0464D4341524401"}'
{"response":"02009000"}

The bridge serves POST /apdu, POST /reset and GET /health on 127.0.0.1.

host/
# a 4-guardian federation runs inside the tests
$ cd host
$ cargo test --workspace

# choose what the host code talks to
$ CARD_BACKEND=soft   # in-process card
$ CARD_BACKEND=bridge # the jCardSim bridge
$ CARD_BACKEND=pcsc   # a reader, with the pcsc feature

The host workspace pins Rust 1.91.1 and Fedimint v0.13.0-beta.1.

applet/
# build the CAP with the Java Card 3.0.5 SDK
$ ant cap -Djc.sdk=$HOME/.javacard/sdks/jc305u4_kit

# install on a blank J3R180 with its default keys
$ gp --install target/fedimint-card-0.1.cap --applet F0464D434152444D
$ gp --create F0464D4341524401 --package F0464D43415244 --applet F0464D4341524401
$ gp --apdu 00A4040008F0464D4341524401   # answers 02009000

Each failed attempt with wrong keys counts toward locking the card for good, so never retry gp on a card whose keys you don't know. On an ACR122U, add --bs 64. To issue cards, use the provisioner app, which replaces the default keys with per-card ones. The CAP build guide has the details.

09

Known limits

  • 32 slots, so at most 32 notes, and a payment's change has to fit in the free ones.
  • There is no PIN unblock, and the owner cannot sign a PIN change.
  • The applet is meant for contactless use. Some commands may stall on a T=0 contact reader.
  • Offline payments need applet 3.0 and settle when the till reconnects. The POS phone needs to reach its till.
